findings.text: Device receive buffer allocation with no bound device, delegating length handling to the generic device allocator.
Aligned receive allocators request extra head space and reserve it on success, with caller flag and atomic convenience forms.
Fragment storage release helper forwarding an address to the page fragment release path.
Poll mode fragment allocators provide sized storage with default or requested alignment, warning on invalid alignment selection.
Device page allocators request receive pages with compound and emergency reserve allowances from no fixed node, with order, single page and atomic convenience forms.
Driver facing receive acquisition entry points for buffers, pages and fragments.
A receive page is reusable only when its node matches the current memory node and it lacks emergency reserve marking.
Memory node query has two configurations, one using per processor state and one using the generic node identity.
Emergency reserve status moves from page to buffer flag only when the source page carries it.
Fragment descriptor holds an offset and a unified backing reference, with helpers to read, adjust, assign and copy each field.
Fragment backing views are exclusive: a type test selects network object versus page interpretation and each view returns absent when asked for the other form.
Fragment address helpers combine stored offset with mapped page base, yielding absent for non page backing or missing mappings, with a safe form rechecking validity and a physical address form.

Fragment device mapping uses a stored device address plus offsets for network object backing and page mapping otherwise, with macro overloads supplying default offset, remainder length and transmit direction.
Partial copy helpers duplicate header area while preserving current headroom, with a clone oriented fast path variant.
Cloned buffer writability requires unshared header and enough preserved header room, with a try helper expanding head when cloned but not writable.
Copy on write delegates with clone state as sharing signal, and pad extends short buffers to a target length with immediate success when already long enough.

Coalescing is refused for zero copy buffers and otherwise allowed only on exact continuation of reference and offset from the prior fragment, with a page wrapper converting to unified reference first.
Linearization collapses paged length into linear area, with forms that skip linear buffers, report shared fragment state, or also handle cloned buffers.

Checksum state on header pull and push keeps complete, partial and none discipline: complete values are arithmetically adjusted while partial with negative start demotes to none, and push plus adjust is offered as one step.
Length trim and grow clear complete checksum state before resizing, with a fast trim path succeeding without work when the target is not shorter.
Queue and tree traversal covers forward, reverse, safe and continued iteration over buffers, with node to buffer conversion and first, last, next and previous access.
Fragment list handling initializes an empty list and iterates chained buffers through successor links.
Datagram and message copy helpers move data between buffers and message iterators, reporting a fault indication when transfers are incomplete.

Header access returns a direct pointer inside linear area, otherwise copies paged range into caller storage or reports absence, with careful and linear only variants adding headroom and bounds checks.
Transmit linearization is needed only for nonlinear buffers whose list or fragment use exceeds device capabilities; linear copy helpers move fixed ranges at base or offset in either direction.

Time access exposes buffer time directly and as old and new timeval and timespec forms, while delivery setters assign time with explicit domain or derive domain from clock identity with warning and zeroing on unknown identity.

Delivery clearing resets domain to realtime and either refreshes stamp when global stamping is required or zeroes it; plain clear and read act only when no delivery domain is set, with conditional read falling back to current time.
Metadata comparison signals difference on unequal present lengths or differing trailing bytes, using wide word accumulation for supported sizes and byte comparison otherwise.
Transmit clone and receive defer timestamp helpers are inert defaults, with software stamping invoked only when software or filtering flags are set.

Unnecessary checksum tracking uses a level count that validation consumes, increment raises or establishes within a maximum, and reset or decrement lowers or clears; full computation is skipped when validity is already assured and complete state can be unset.
Receive checksum breakpoint threshold equals seventy six.
Invalid fragment alignment choice triggers a one time warning and proceeds with transformed value, so callers must supply valid alignment.
Fragment address derivation can be absent for alternate backing or unmapped pages, so callers must validate before use.
Header retrieval outside linear area needs caller scratch space and can fail, including negative offsets beyond available headroom.
